title: Adaptive Residual-Update Steering for Low-Overhead Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
claim: Existing non-steering and steering methods lack adaptive, low-overhead control; ours fixes hallucination while matching baseline cost.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: example image, text outputs, checkmark comparison table
description: A wide three-part figure. On the left, a photo of a man standing in a dim room facing a TV, with a prompt box below asking the model to describe the image in detail. In the middle, two stacked text bubbles. The salmon bubble is the vanilla output, and its hallucinated phrase 'a cup placed on a surface' is in red with a ghost emoji. The green bubble is RUDDER's output, with its corrected factual phrase in blue and a smiley emoji. On the right is a feature-comparison table with columns Non-steering (gray), Steering-based (blue) and Ours: RUDDER (green). Rows are No Extra FWD, Per-token Adaptive, Answer-span Localized, No Offline Setup and Typical Overhead. Red crosses and green checkmarks fill the cells, so RUDDER's column is all checks. The last row reads High, Mid-High and ≈Baseline.
caption: (Left) An example where the vanilla LLaVA-1.5--7B [ref] hallucinates objects. Erroneous text is marked in red, while RUDDER's corrected, factual output is in blue. (Right) A comparison showing that unlike existing non-steering and steering-based methods, RUDDER provides adaptive, low-overhead control without requiring extra forward passes.
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) typically process visual inputs as a prefix to the language decoder. As the model autoregressively generates text, this initial visual information inevitably undergoes "dilution" leading the model to over-rely on language priors and hallucinate objects. Existing interventions attempt to correct this by contrasting logits or iteratively refining outputs, but they incur prohibitive latency costs. We propose Residual-Update Directed DEcoding Regulation (RUDDER), a framework that counters visual dilution by creating a persistent visual anchor. We extract a robust evidence direction (CARD) directly from the model's prefill residual updates, and inject it into the decoding process. This injection is modulated by an adaptive gate, the Beta Gate, which acts as a trust mechanism and ensures the visual reminder is applied only when necessary. Experiments on LLaVA-1.5 (7B/13B), Idefics2, InstructBLIP, and Qwen2.5-VL demonstrate that RUDDER consistently mitigates hallucination (with greedy decoding, RUDDER reduces CHAIR_S by an average of 24.4% and CHAIR_i by 23.6% relative) and scales effectively across architectures, all while maintaining >96.0% throughput.
